# Branch review: `fix-checkpoint-trailer-block`

**Verdict: request changes**

Scope: `main...fix-checkpoint-trailer-block` at `2d16b3666`, covering one commit and seven changed files.

## Author intent

The change separates two meanings that the old checkpoint parser conflated:

- Whole-message parsing remains available for historical discovery, especially GitHub and native Git squash commits containing several embedded checkpoint trailers.
- Final-trailer-block parsing authorizes checkpoint creation, reuse, and mutation.

That split is the right design. The hook and attach changes apply it in several important places without breaking the existing squash-resume tests. The implementation is not complete, however: two mutation paths still trust whole-message results, and the strict parser does not match Git's trailer grammar.

No pull request currently exists for this branch. The related [PR #2168](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2168) remains open.

## Spec

### Act on

#### High: `checkpoint explain --commit ... --generate` can write to a body-selected checkpoint

[`runExplainAuto`](cmd/entire/cli/explain.go#L617) and [`runExplainCommit`](cmd/entire/cli/explain.go#L2994) still resolve commit linkage with whole-message `ParseCheckpoint`. When `--generate` is present, that ID reaches [`store.Write`](cmd/entire/cli/explain.go#L1095).

A commit body can therefore name an existing but unrelated checkpoint and cause:

```text
commit body
    -> ParseCheckpoint(existing ID)
    -> checkpoint explain --generate --force
    -> generateCheckpointSummary
    -> store.Write(existing ID)
```

This violates the recorded requirement to "prevent untrusted checkpoint-shaped commit-body text from being accepted in unsafe contexts."

Use final-block parsing when commit resolution leads to summary generation. Keep whole-message parsing only for read-only discovery. Add regressions for both explicit `--commit` and positional commit fallback.

#### Medium: legacy migration still lets body text authorize reconciliation

[`migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded`](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_migration.go#L72) scans the whole message when a legacy state lacks `LastCheckpointCommitHash`. A matching body ID advances both `BaseCommit` and `AttributionBaseCommit`, skipping normal migration and changing future attribution.

This conflicts with the intended boundary that body IDs are discovery candidates while final-block IDs authorize mutation.

Require final-block evidence for the legacy fallback, or decline reconciliation when the recorded commit hash is unavailable. Add a legacy-state regression with a matching body ID followed by a different final trailer block.

### Consider

None.

### Noted

The existing squash-history semantics are preserved. All three named squash-resume unit tests passed unchanged.

### Dismissed

None.

**Worst spec issue:** `--generate` can persist a summary to a checkpoint selected solely by commit-body text.

## Standards

### Act on

#### High: leading whitespace turns body text into an authorizing trailer

[`ParseAllCheckpointsFromFinalTrailerBlock`](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go#L162) and [`finalTrailerBlock`](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go#L306) left-trim lines before classifying and parsing them.

This line is therefore accepted:

```text
  Entire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6
```

Git 2.50's `git interpret-trailers --parse` returns no trailer for the same message. The branch parser nevertheless lets that line choose the ID used by PostCommit condensation and attach.

Do not remove leading spaces or tabs when validating final-block trailer lines. Add production-path regressions for PostCommit and attach, not only parser tests.

#### Medium: commit-message comment handling does not follow Git configuration

[`parseCheckpointFromCommitMessageFile`](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go#L290) strips only `#` suffix lines. Git permits a configurable `core.commentChar`, and default cleanup preserves comment-prefixed lines when no editor runs. See the official [`git commit` cleanup documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit/2.52.0).

This creates two failure shapes:

- A repository using another comment character can hide a legitimate final trailer behind Git's comment block.
- A `git commit -m` or `-F` message can contain real `#` user content that this helper discards before deciding an earlier checkpoint-shaped body line is final.

Resolve Git's effective comment character or apply Git-equivalent cleanup rules. Cover editor, `-m`/`-F`, and custom-comment-character flows.

### Consider

#### Support Git trailer continuations

[`finalTrailerBlock`](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go#L317) walks backward only while every line independently matches `Key: value`. Git accepts continuation lines beginning with whitespace, so a multiline trailer after `Entire-Checkpoint` can make the branch parser reject the entire block even though Git accepts it.

This may produce a duplicate checkpoint ID during prepare/amend or make PostCommit skip condensation. Either support continuation lines or explicitly document and test the narrower grammar.

#### Exercise attach through its durable boundary

`TestAttachIgnoresCheckpointShapedBodyText` calls `resolveCheckpointID` and `promptAmendCommit` separately. It does not prove through `runAttach` that a forged checkpoint remains unmodified and a fresh checkpoint receives the attached session.

A full-path regression should inspect the persistent store after attach.

### Noted

- The strict maintainability pass found no structural regression. The large hook file was already over 1,000 lines; this change did not cross that threshold or scatter the core parser policy.
- The parser change adds no lock or interruption point. Parser selection occurs before existing writes, so cleanup and recovery semantics are otherwise unchanged.
- Median `PrepareCommitMsg` time was 15.20 ms on this branch versus 15.13 ms on `main`, a difference of roughly 0.5% and within sample noise.

### Dismissed

One adversarial reviewer flagged `hasUserContent` for treating every checkpoint-shaped line as Entire metadata. That behavior predates this branch and requires a commit whose only user content is itself checkpoint-shaped. It is not a regression introduced here.

**Worst standards issue:** the strict parser accepts a Git-invalid indented body line as mutation authority.

## Correctness model

### Who owns each write?

- PrepareCommitMsg chooses the checkpoint ID; PostCommit owns condensation into persistent checkpoint storage.
- Attach chooses or reuses an ID, writes the attached session, then best-effort amends the commit.
- `checkpoint explain --generate` owns summary persistence.
- Session migration owns `BaseCommit` and `AttributionBaseCommit` reconciliation.

The first two owners now use the strict parser in their main paths. Summary generation and legacy migration do not.

### What happens around interruption?

The diff changes classification before existing writes. It does not add a lock, subprocess, temporary file, or new partial-write state. Existing write and recovery owners remain responsible before and after the decision. The outstanding risk is wrong-target mutation, not new interruption behavior.

### Which tests observe the real contract?

- The PrepareCommitMsg regression enters the production hook and would fail on the old code.
- The attach test observes helpers rather than the durable store contract.
- No regression covers body-selected summary generation, legacy migration, indented pseudo-trailers, custom Git comment characters, or trailer continuation lines.

## Multi-model agreement

Three independent reviewers examined the same intent and diff:

| Finding | Agreement | Disposition |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Explain generation trusts body IDs | 3/3 | Act on |
| Indented pseudo-trailer accepted | 2/3 | Act on |
| Legacy migration trusts body IDs | 2/3 | Act on |
| Git comment handling is hard-coded | 1/3 | Act on after local verification |
| `hasUserContent` removes body-shaped lines | 1/3 | Dismissed as pre-existing |

## Verification performed

- Focused trailer parser tests passed.
- Focused PrepareCommitMsg and attach tests passed.
- `TestFindCheckpointInHistory_MultipleCheckpoints` passed.
- `TestFindBranchCheckpoint_SquashMergeMultipleCheckpoints` passed.
- `TestResumeFromCurrentBranch_MultipleCheckpointsSaysLatest` passed.
- `git diff --check main..HEAD` passed.
- Git 2.50 rejected indented pseudo-trailers and accepted continuation-line trailer blocks in direct `git interpret-trailers --parse` checks.
- Checkpoint history records a successful pre-commit `mise run check`; the full gate was not rerun during this read-only review.

## Recommendation

Request changes. Close the two remaining mutation paths first, then make the strict parser agree with Git about indentation and comment cleanup. Preserve whole-message discovery for squash history throughout.

{"body":"Fixes #2255
Fixes #2256

An `Entire-Checkpoint:` line anywhere in a commit message still decides which checkpoint a commit writes to. Main's provenance check (`stampedByAnotherCommit`) only refuses a checkpoint that already exists in the local store, so a checkpoint ID in a commit body, whether pasted, quoted, indented, or mentioned mid-sentence, still steers three writes.

This PR now also carries #2259 (the trailer writer fix). The stricter reader here is what makes that writer bug reachable, so the two need to land together, and I'm closing #2259 in favour of this one.

## Problem

I ported the scenarios onto current main and ran them there:

| Scenario on main | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `entire attach` on a commit whose body says `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` | The attached session is written into `<id>`, which ends up holding two unrelated sessions. Same for an indented line and for "Follow-up to Entire-Checkpoint: <id> from last week." |
| `git commit -m` with that line in the body, `<id>` not in this clone | prepare-commit-msg treats it as already stamped and adds no trailer. Post-commit then condenses the session's work under `<id>`, claiming an ID that may belong to a teammate's unfetched checkpoint. |
| Same, `<id>` already in this clone | Post-commit correctly refuses to write there, but the commit ends up with no checkpoint at all. |
| `entire explain --commit <sha> --generate` | Resolves the first mention anywhere in the message. |

## Cause

Every place that decides "may I write to this checkpoint" reads trailers with `ParseCheckpoint`/`ParseAllCheckpoints`, whose regex is unanchored and scans the whole message. That is right for discovery, since squash commits carry their squashed commits' trailers in the body, and wrong for deciding a write.

## Fix

Only the final trailer block, read by git's grammar, decides a write:

- `stampedTrailer` (prepare-commit-msg and the agent fast path) and `stampedTrailersOf` (post-commit)
- the amend handler, which still treats a deleted ID mentioned anywhere as stripped, as main does
- attach's `planAttachLink` and `resolveCheckpointID`, switched together so joining and resolving agree
- explain's `--generate` paths, and the per-commit read-only views (`explain <commit>`, `explain --commit`, the export, and the review re-run guard), which now show the checkpoint `--generate` and attach use (`CommitCheckpoint`: the final block's last ID, falling back to the first ID anywhere only when the block names none)

Prepare reads the message as git will record it. Git runs its commit hooks with `GIT_EDITOR=:` when it opens no editor (githooks(5): `-m`/`-F` without `-e`, `--no-edit`, `-C`), which the source word cannot tell, since `-m -e` reports `message` and an amend reports `commit` either way. A message git opens loses the lines starting with git's comment prefix and everything from the exact scissors line down; any other keeps its comment lines, unless `commit.cleanup=strip`. Git's comment block is the run of comment lines after a blank line that ends the message, or the part above the scissors line, which can also start it. The prefix is `core.commentChar` or `core.commentString` (aliases, last one set wins), `#` when unset, and for `auto` it is read back from that block, checked against git's own rule, or, with no block (`commit.status=false`, no editor), picked by that rule: the first of `#;@!$%^&|:` that starts no line. Prepare then judges the final block as post-commit will read the recorded commit, by git's trailer grammar with `auto` read as `#`. Prepare writes its explanation and inherited trailers with the same prefix, so git's cleanup removes the explanation. Trailer lines accept `Key:value` and tab separators, as git does. The final-block reader rejects leading-whitespace pseudo-trailers, accepts indented lines only as continuations, never reads the subject paragraph as trailers, and skips lines starting with git's comment prefix, as git's trailer parser does. That last part matters because `commit.cleanup=scissors` and `whitespace` keep comment lines, so the recorded commit carries Entire's explanation right below its trailer. Post-commit, attach and `explain --generate` read a recorded commit with the configured prefix (`auto` reads as `#`, as in `git interpret-trailers`), and only look the prefix up when the message names a checkpoint that a read without it misses. The writer from #2259 joins only a trailer block without comment lines, so a trailer it appends is always one the readers accept.

Every trailer prepare adds to a message git opens goes above git's comment block, whether it is the template's, an amend's restored or fresh one, an agent's, or an inherited one, so `commit -v` cannot cut it off. Under `auto` with a cleanup that keeps comment lines, git's block would stay below the trailer where the grammar does not skip it, so the trailer goes below the block instead, above any scissors line. A message git does not open gets its trailer appended, so its own lines stay where the user put them (`-m "#42 fix login"`, `--amend --no-edit` of a body ending in a `#` paragraph). The template puts prepare's explanation in its own paragraph between the user's lines and the trailer: a subject typed on the line just above cannot join the trailer into the subject paragraph, and cleanup modes that keep comments leave the trailer as its own block. Like git, the reader also accepts a block holding a `Signed-off-by:` or `(cherry picked from commit …)` line with other lines in it, while trailers make up at least a quarter of the block. `explain --generate` writes into the block's last ID, the one attach joins, and when the only checkpoint lines sit outside the final block its error names them. Post-commit also accepts the trailer prepare left, stamped, restored or kept, wherever the user's edits moved it (a per-worktree marker tied to the commit's parent): prepare generated that ID or found it in the final block it was handed, so an ID pasted into the body cannot match it. prepare-commit-msg reads git's comment config once per hook.

The commit-msg hook's empty-message check now counts content the way git's cleanup will, from the same `GIT_EDITOR` signal: prefix lines count as comments only in a message git opened, or in every message under `commit.cleanup=strip`, which git applies to `-m` messages too, using the same comment prefix and exact scissors line. A `Signed-off-by:` line alone is not content, as in git's own check. Before, an untouched editor message with `core.commentChar=;` or `commit -v` was committed holding only the trailer instead of aborting, and `git commit -m "#42 fix login"` lost its trailer; both also happen on main.

Unchanged on purpose: read-only lookups that discover every checkpoint a commit mentions (resume, status, attribution, explain's history listings), squash and redo inheritance, and `RemoveCheckpointTrailers`, which stays broad so a delete removes every copy.

## Why nothing caught it

Main already stops a leftover mention of a deleted checkpoint from counting as the commit's own (`TestCheckpointDelete_LeftoverDeletedIDNeverReceivesNewWork`), by filtering through the deleted list. The same leftover naming a live or unfetched checkpoint was not covered, and attach and explain had no test with a body mention at all.

The branch's own tests then simulated git: they handed the hooks the message git would write and recorded commits with go-git, so they shared the code's assumptions about git's comment block and editor, and each review round found another git mode. `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits` now runs real `git commit` with Entire's hooks and a scripted editor.

## Tests, verified RED before the fix

Each failed on main's call sites (I merged main first) and passes now:

- **Body mentions:** `checkpoint_trailer_authority_test.go` (real hook binaries), `TestAttach_*DoesNotSelectCheckpoint` and `TestExplainGenerate_BodyCheckpointLineIsNotATrailer`. A pasted, indented or prose `Entire-Checkpoint:` line is no longer reused by prepare, joined by attach, or written by `explain --generate`.
- **Comment prefix and scissors:** `EditorCommitHonorsCommentChar`, `AmendHonorsCommentChar`, `ProseScissorsMarkerIsNotACut`, `UntouchedEditorMessageAborts` and `MessageSubjectStartingWithHashKeepsTrailer`. `;`, `auto`, `commit -v` and `-m "#42 …"` messages are read the way git cleans them.
- **Cleanup modes that keep comments:** `CleanupKeepingCommentsLinksTheCommit` and `TestAttach_TrailerFollowedByCommentLinesJoinsCheckpoint`. With `commit.cleanup=scissors` or `whitespace` the trailer still links the commit, as `git interpret-trailers` reads it.
- **Grammar:** `trailers_test.go` covers the subject paragraph, continuations, `Key:value` and tab separators, and comment lines.

`VerboseAmendKeepsItsTrailer` and `TestExplainReadOnly_FindsBodyCheckpointLine` are guards that pass before and after.

Review then found regressions in the stricter rule itself; these failed on the branch before their fix:

- **Trailers prepare adds:** `AddedTrailerSurvivesVerboseCleanup` (amend restore, amend after a delete, agent editor commit), `ClearedAmendMessageAborts`, `SubjectOnTheTemplatesSecondLineLinks`, the `auto` row of `CleanupKeepingCommentsLinksTheCommit`, and the `AnchorsToTheEndingBlock` unit tests. `UntouchedEditorMessageAborts` gains a `commit.status=false` guard.
- **Git's block rule and explain:** the cherry-pick and quarter-trailer cases in `trailers_test.go`, and `TestExplainGenerate_UsesTheLastFinalBlockTrailer`.
- **`commit.cleanup=strip` and scissors:** `StripCleanupMessageOfCommentsAborts`, and the CRLF scissors case in `trailers_test.go`, where git does not cut.

A second review round found more git modes; these failed on the branch before their fix:

- **Real git:** `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits`, 15 `git commit` cases across `-m`, `-m -e -v`, `-F`, the editor, `--amend`, `--amend --no-edit`, templates, `;`, `auto`, `commit.status=false` and the strip, whitespace and scissors cleanups. Each commit must end with exactly the trailer prepare left as its final block, stored by post-commit, keep the user's lines first, and abort when saved untouched. Before the fix, `-F` under `auto` got a second trailer, and a template under `auto` with whitespace cleanup ended with git's `;` block below its trailer.
- **Placement:** `NoEditAmendKeepsHashLinesInPlace` (the restored trailer landed above `#42 fix login`), `MessageEndingWithHashLinesKeepsItsParagraphs`, the `-m -e -v` row of `AddedTrailerSurvivesVerboseCleanup` (the trailer went below the diff), `BodyTypedBelowTheTrailerStillLinks` (agent fast path and amend keep), and the `AutoCommentPrefix` and `StampedTrailer` unit tests.
- **Readers:** `TestExplainReadOnly_ShowsTheLastFinalBlockTrailer`, `TestRunExplainExport_CommitExportsItsLastFinalTrailer` (it exported `aaaaaaaaaaaa` instead of `bbbbbbbbbbbb`) and `TestHeadCheckpointFlags_ReadsTheFinalBlockTrailer`. `TestExplainGenerate_BodyCheckpointLineIsNotATrailer` now expects the error to name the checkpoint.

Also added with these fixes: `EditedMessageSourceKeepsGitsBlockLast`, `MessageEndingWithHashLineLinks`, `BodyTypedBelowTemplatePromptStillLinks`, `AutoCommentCharWithoutStatusBlock` and `CommitMsgFollowsGitsEmptinessRules`.

## Rejected alternatives

- Anchoring the whole-message regex to line starts: a body line could still steer writes, and indented squash messages would stop being discovered.
- Checking only that the named checkpoint exists: existence says nothing about whether this commit stamped it, and it misses IDs this clone has not fetched.
- Guessing `auto` from the whole message: once git has written its comment block, the character it chose always looks used, so the guess is wrong. The prefix is read back from git's own block instead.
- Guessing whether git opened the editor from the source word or the message's shape: `-m -e` reports `message`, an amend reports `commit` either way, and a `-m` message can end with `#` lines that look like git's block. Git tells its hooks with `GIT_EDITOR=:`.
- Splitting the stricter reader from the placement fixes: the reader alone loses the link in every mode where main's writer leaves the trailer outside the final block, so they ship together.

## Known gap

A commit whose stamped trailer the user moves out of the final block in the editor, for example by typing a body below it, is still condensed into that checkpoint: post-commit accepts the trailer prepare left. Attach and `explain --generate` read only the final block, so they treat that commit as unlinked, and `--generate` names the out-of-block checkpoint in its error. Moving the trailer back would take a new step in commit-msg, so it is left out.

The hooks read git's `GIT_EDITOR=:` as "no editor". A `GIT_EDITOR=:` you export yourself looks the same, so such a commit gets its trailer after git's comment block (lost with `-v`), and a message saved untouched is recorded holding only the trailer instead of aborting.

`explain`'s history listings still match a commit by the first checkpoint ID in its message.

Squash and redo inheritance still scan the whole message of the squashed or reset commits, so an `Entire-Checkpoint:` mention in one of their bodies is carried into the new commit's final trailer block. Fixing it needs per-commit parsing of SQUASH_MSG and a rule for nested squashes, so it is left for a follow-up.

A GitHub "Squash and merge" commit joins the squashed messages without indentation, so its final block is the last squashed commit's trailer and attach joins that checkpoint, as on main. Telling it apart needs a way to recognize squash merges.

## Branch history

This branch predates main's provenance model. I merged current main, resolved every call-site conflict to main's version (the legacy migration this PR used to touch is gone), and re-applied the final-block reads to main's call sites in the last commit. The diff against main is the change to review.

# General Review Lessons

- Make a guard's zero-match check count only the matches it is meant to protect. Matches that are always present, like the guard's own allowed cases, keep the check from ever firing.
- Test a guard by planting a violation and by breaking its detection, and see it fail both times. A guard that passes on clean code proves nothing.
- Before acting on a review finding, check whether existing tests or contracts explain the current shape. A structural test can be why the code looks the way it does.
- When code reads a user-owned config into a typed struct and writes it back, keep the fields it does not model. Any new reason to rewrite the file otherwise silently deletes user data.
- Make a new outer timeout longer than every internal budget on that path. Otherwise the kill fires before the code's own graceful fallback.
- Before setting an explicit timeout, look up the platform's current default for that exact event; an explicit value can shorten the budget rather than add one.
- When splitting known from unknown JSON keys to preserve them, decode only the exact known keys and keep every other key, case variants included, as unknown. `encoding/json` matches field names case-insensitively, so decoding the whole object lets a key like `"Command"` overwrite the real field.
- When a change makes a fix command riskier, changes which command to run, or adds a new place that reports an existing failure, check every place that already reports it (status, doctor, enable, help text) so they all give the same fix. Otherwise one screen sends people to the safe fix and the next to the destructive one, or one command prints the same failure twice with different fixes.
- When a test plants a failure to cover an error branch, make sure an earlier step doesn't fail first; otherwise the assertion passes without ever running that branch.
- Select an agent's final report by a marker it carries (such as the contract line), not by its position in the event stream; a trailing tool call or an empty message ID moves a position-based boundary.
- When code keeps state so a later run can retry, test the retry itself. A test that checks the kept state against the same expression the code uses would pass even if that expression were wrong.
- When decoding user-editable JSON into maps or pointers, skip null elements before writing to them; `[null]` decodes to a nil map and a write panics.
- Review a PR that is behind main against current main, not its own base: build both and run the same repro. Its tests pass on its old base even when keeping its side of a conflict would undo a fix merged since.
- When wiring user config into a new path, test it with a broken config too. A user rule that silently fails to load leaks the same way as one that was never wired.
- Make a fail-closed check fire only on the failure it guards against, not on a whole class of errors. A refusal on any settings error blocks unrelated cases and pushes users toward a less safe escape hatch, such as an unredacted `--raw` bundle.
- Read the Trail's current description and resolved findings before drafting review comments. The trail description can be newer than the PR description and may already list known follow-ups, which turns "you missed this" into a question about scale or timing.
- When a PR claims corpus validation, check what the corpus contained, and test on inputs from outside it, such as other languages and other codebases. A corpus drawn from one codebase can pass while common idioms elsewhere break.
- When a PR adds a second implementation of an existing contract, such as another way to compute an offset or boundary, check it uses the same rule as the existing path and test it with input that hits the contract's edge case. A mock that maps input one-to-one passes whichever rule is used.
- Don't rewrite a value before other detectors scan it; collect detections on the unchanged value and merge them. Masking first can break anchored or overlapping matches and expose text the old pipeline redacted.

Forged `Entire-Checkpoint` lines in commit bodies can select and mutate unrelated checkpoints
OPEN
## Summary

Checkpoint resolution parses trailers out of the whole commit message, including in code paths that decide whether to create, reuse, or mutate checkpoint storage. A line shaped like `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` anywhere in the body is indistinguishable from a real squashed trailer. So a commit body that names an existing checkpoint ID, whether pasted, reverted, or written by someone else, gets treated as authority over that checkpoint.

## Impact

A commit body naming an existing checkpoint ID can:

- make PostCommit condensation bind the commit to a checkpoint that has nothing to do with it, instead of minting a fresh one
- make `entire checkpoint attach` write the attached session into the unrelated checkpoint
- make `entire checkpoint explain --commit ... --generate` persist a generated summary into it via `store.Write`
- make legacy session migration (`migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded`) advance `BaseCommit` and `AttributionBaseCommit` off a body ID, skipping normal migration and changing future attribution

Checking that the ID exists in storage doesn't help. Existence proves nothing about the ID's relationship to this commit.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Work in a repo with Entire enabled, in an agent session that has already produced at least one checkpoint. Note an existing checkpoint ID from `entire checkpoint list` (call it `<unrelated-id>`).
2. Make an unrelated code change in a new agent session.
3. Commit it with a message whose body contains a checkpoint-shaped line naming the existing ID:

   ```sh
   git commit -m "innocent change

   Entire-Checkpoint: <unrelated-id>"
   ```

4. Let the PostCommit hook run, then inspect `entire checkpoint list` and the commit's linkage.

`AppendCheckpointTrailer` can emit a trailer the final-block parser (and git) reject
OPEN
## Summary

`trailers.appendTrailerLine` (the writer behind `AppendCheckpointTrailer` and `AppendOPFAppliedTrailer`) and `trailers.finalTrailerBlock` (the reader behind the strict `ParseCheckpointFromFinalTrailerBlock` / `ParseAllCheckpointsFromFinalTrailerBlock` parsers introduced in #2253) implement two different grammars for "is this paragraph a trailer block". When a commit message ends with an indented checkpoint-shaped line, the writer joins a real trailer onto that paragraph without a separating blank line, producing a message in which **neither our strict readers nor git itself** can see the trailer that was just appended. The CLI reports success while every downstream hook silently ignores the commit.

The reader's grammar matches git's; the writer is the buggy side.

## The grammar divergence

**Writer** (`cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go`, `appendTrailerLine`): to decide whether the message already ends in a trailer block, it takes the last non-comment line and tests `IsTrailerLine(strings.TrimSpace(line))`. The `TrimSpace` means an indented line like `␣␣Entire-Checkpoint: A` — which is *not* a trailer to git — passes the check. It then walks upward, again trimming each line, until it finds a blank line, and concludes "trailer block present, join directly".

**Reader** (`finalTrailerBlock`): isolates the final paragraph and accepts it only if every line is either a real trailer line (`IsTrailerLine` on the **raw** line — leading whitespace fails the `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*: ` regex) or an indented continuation *of a preceding trailer*. An indented line at the top of the paragraph has nothing to continue, so the entire paragraph is rejected and the parsers return nothing. This intentionally mirrors git, which treats an indented line after a trailer as a continuation of that trailer's value, never as a new trailer.

So the writer's membership test is strictly looser than the reader's, and the looseness is load-bearing: it changes where the writer places the new trailer.

## Reproduction

Start from a commit message whose final paragraph is an indented checkpoint-shaped line — for example one pasted from attach's own non-interactive hint, which prints the trailer with a two-space indent (`Copy to your commit message to attach:\n\n  Entire-Checkpoint: <id>`):

```
Message

Body.

  Entire-Checkpoint: <A>
```

// gitCommentPrefix must name the prefix git's own cleanup uses, or prepare reads

func TestGitCommentPrefix(t *testing.T) {
	testutil.IsolateGitConfigEnv(t)
	dir := resolvedTempDir(t)
	testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)
	t.Chdir(dir)
	ctx := context.Background()
	const semicolonBlock = "# Release notes\n\n; Please enter the commit message for your changes.\n;\n"

	require.Equal(t, "#", gitCommentConfig(ctx).prefixFor("Subject\n", true), "unset")

	testutil.RunGit(t, dir, "config", "core.commentChar", ";")
	require.Equal(t, ";", gitCommentConfig(ctx).prefixFor("Subject\n", true))

	testutil.RunGit(t, dir, "config", "core.commentString", "//")
	require.Equal(t, "//", gitCommentConfig(ctx).prefixFor("Subject\n", true), "the two keys are aliases: the last one set wins")

	testutil.RunGit(t, dir, "config", "--unset", "core.commentChar")
	testutil.RunGit(t, dir, "config", "core.commentChar", "@")
	require.Equal(t, "@", gitCommentConfig(ctx).prefixFor("Subject\n", true), "the two keys are aliases: the last one set wins")

	testutil.RunGit(t, dir, "config", "--unset", "core.commentString")
	testutil.RunGit(t, dir, "config", "core.commentChar", "auto")
	require.Equal(t, ";", gitCommentConfig(ctx).prefixFor(semicolonBlock, true), "auto: the prefix git's comment block was written with")
	require.Equal(t, "#", gitCommentConfig(ctx).prefixFor("Subject\n", true), "auto without a comment block")

	cancelled, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	cancel()
	require.Equal(t, "#", gitCommentConfig(cancelled).prefixFor(semicolonBlock, true), "an unreadable config falls back to git's default")
}

content.text:
**PR 2253 at head 89af8a14e is close to ready.** I didn't change any repo files. CI is green, it merges cleanly with current main, and real `git commit` probes found no new link losses. Before approval it needs two small fixes: a unit test that depends on the developer's `GIT_EDITOR`, and a comment that names a function that no longer exists.

## Brief

**What it does:** only the commit's final trailer block can decide which checkpoint a commit writes to. That covers prepare-commit-msg, post-commit, attach and `explain --generate`. An `Entire-Checkpoint:` line anywhere else (pasted, quoted, indented, or in a sentence) can no longer send a session's work into an unrelated checkpoint (#2255).

**How:** the hooks now read the message the way git will record it:
- They tell whether git opened the editor from `GIT_EDITOR=:`, which git sets for its hooks when it doesn't.
- They read the comment prefix from git config (`core.commentChar`/`commentString`, `auto`, `commit.cleanup`, `commit.status`).
- Every trailer they add goes where git's cleanup leaves it in the final block.
- A small per-worktree marker lets post-commit keep the trailer prepare stamped even when the user's edits move it out of the final block.
- The trailer writer from #2259 is folded in.

**What this commit adds:** the `GIT_EDITOR` signal, the stamp marker, consistent last-ID reads in explain/export/review guard, and `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits` (15 real `git commit` cases).

**Risk:** behaviour is unchanged for normal `-m` and editor commits. It changes for comment-prefix configs, cleanup modes and a few edge cases. The cost is extra git subprocesses in the commit hooks (numbers below).

**Lookups:**
- No Trail is discoverable for the branch.
- `entire checkpoint explain 89af8a14e` shows the commit was requested by another session; it has no summary.
- `entire search` turned up this branch's earlier rounds and main's "Place inherited trailers above git's comment block".
- The linked issues are #2255 and #2256.
- `librarian` failed with an HTTP 302 (VPN), so I have no Linear or Slack context.
- I didn't run `entire graph impact`.

## Findings

### Act on

1. **A unit test depends on the developer's shell.** `gitOpensEditor()` ([manual_commit_hooks.go:2988](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:2988)) reads `GIT_EDITOR` from the process. Strategy unit tests run the hooks in-process and nothing pins that variable. With `GIT_EDITOR=:` exported (for example, tests run from a pre-commit hook), `TestPrepareCommitMsg_RedoInVerboseEditorKeepsTrailersAboveScissors` fails. With it unset, the test passes. Fix: unset or pin `GIT_EDITOR` in the strategy `TestMain` ([global_test.go:29](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/global_test.go:29)), as the integration harness already does.
2. **References to things that no longer exist:**
   - The doc comment on `addCheckpointTrailerWithComment` ([manual_commit_hooks.go:3175](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:3175)) points to `gitCommentPrefix`, which doesn't exist. So does the comment on `TestGitCommentPrefix` ([manual_commit_test.go:1025](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_test.go:1025)).
   - `TestAddInheritedCheckpointTrailer_*` are named after a function that was removed.

### Consider

3. **Git's command-line `--cleanup` and `--no-status` flags are invisible to the hooks.** Only the config values are read. With `core.commentChar=auto`, a `#` template and `--cleanup=whitespace` on the command line, the recorded commit ends with git's kept `;` block and its final block holds no trailer. Post-commit still condenses through the marker, but attach and `explain --generate` see the commit as unlinked. This is niche, but worth one line in the PR's "Known gap".
4. **Entire's explanation lands in the commit under `whitespace`, `scissors` or `verbatim` cleanup.** This also happens on main. The branch now knows git will keep the comment lines (`rules.stripped == false`), so it can skip the explanation the same way it already does for messages git doesn't open ([manual_commit_hooks.go:611](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:611)).
5. **Hook cost.** I counted git subprocesses with a PATH shim:

   | Hook | main | branch | What's added |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | prepare-commit-msg, linked commit | 7 | 10 | `git config`, plus two uncached `rev-parse --git-dir` for the stamp marker |
   | prepare-commit-msg, every commit | | +1 | `clearStampedTrailer` runs first, even with no session |
   | commit-msg | 0 | 1 | `git config` |
   | post-commit | | +1 | `rev-parse --git-dir` |

   `git config` takes about 8 ms here, so a linked commit costs roughly 25 ms more across the hooks. My timing benchmarks were unreliable (load average 89), so I'm not quoting those. Resolving the per-worktree git root once per hook (`GetGitDir`, [hooks.go:66](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/hooks.go:66), spawns every call) removes most of it.
6. **The new paragraph in [sessions-and-checkpoints.md](docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md:272) is about 60 lines of unbroken text** and largely repeats the PR description. A short list of rules would be easier to maintain.

### Noted

- Real `git commit` probes, run as a scratch overlay test outside the repo, all linked through the final block:
  - `merge --squash`, in the editor and with `--no-edit`
  - `-s`, `-v` and `commit.verbose`
  - `-c core.commentChar=;`
  - `--trailer`, with the editor and with `-m`
  - `--fixup`, `-c HEAD` and a conventional template with comment lines
  - deleting the trailer in the editor correctly unlinks the commit
- Typing a body below the trailer links only through the marker, which is the gap the PR already documents.
- `FinalCheckpointTrailers`' shortcut (read without the comment prefix first) gives the same IDs as git's full rule, so it is safe.

All the findings reproduce on the pushed head (89af8a14e). Here is what I'd change for each. Nothing has been edited yet.

**F1. A unit test depends on your shell's `GIT_EDITOR`.**
- **Problem:** `TestPrepareCommitMsg_RedoInVerboseEditorKeepsTrailersAboveScissors` fails when `GIT_EDITOR=:` is exported and passes when it's unset.
- **Cause:** the hook decides whether git opened the editor by reading `GIT_EDITOR` from the process environment. The strategy unit tests run the hook in the test process and never pin that variable.
- **Change:** unset `GIT_EDITOR` in the strategy `TestMain`, next to the existing git config isolation. Tests only, one line plus a comment.

**F2. Names that point to removed code.**
- **Problem:** two comments mention `gitCommentPrefix`, which no longer exists (one in a production doc comment, one on `TestGitCommentPrefix`). Two tests are named after `addInheritedCheckpointTrailer`, which was removed.
- **Change:** point the comments at what exists now (`commentRules.prefix` / `messageCommentRules`) and rename the tests to match the current functions. No behaviour change.

**F7. New: a template without a final newline, under `auto`, records Entire's explanation in the commit.**
- **Problem:** I reproduced this on the pushed head. The commit records `@ Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer…` lines. It is the case the matrix test in the other clone had to skip.
- **Cause:** when the message has no final newline, git writes its comment block directly under the last line, with no blank line in between. `AutoCommentPrefix` only recognises git's block when a blank line sits above it. So it falls back to scanning the whole message, git's own `;` block included, and picks `@` instead of `;`. git then keeps the `@` lines.
- **Change:** when reading back the prefix under `auto`, accept the run of prefix lines at the end of the message even without a blank line above. This is safe because git picks a character that starts no line of the user's message, so that run can only be git's own block. Test first: add an `AutoCommentPrefix` unit case and a row to `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits`, see both fail, then fix.

**F4. Under `whitespace`, `scissors` or `verbatim` cleanup, every editor commit records Entire's explanation.**
- **Problem:** this already happens on main.
- **Cause:** the explanation is written whenever git opens the editor, even when Entire knows git will keep comment lines (`rules.stripped == false`).
- **Change:** skip the explanation in that case, as the code already does for messages git doesn't open. Test first: assert "Entire's explanation is never recorded" across the real-git table, which fails on the whitespace and scissors rows.
- **Tradeoff:** people using those cleanup modes lose the "remove this trailer to unlink" hint in the editor.

**F5. Each linked commit costs about 4 more git processes than on main.**
- **Problem:** prepare-commit-msg goes from 7 to 10 git processes, commit-msg from 0 to 1, and post-commit adds 1. Every prepare adds 1 even when there is no session.
- **Cause:** each marker read or write resolves the git dir again with `git rev-parse --git-dir`, and that lookup isn't cached.
- **Change:** resolve the git dir once per hook and keep it on the hook's context, the same way the comment config is already read once per hook. That leaves only the `git config` read as new cost. I'll check with the before/after process count.

**F3 + F6. Docs.**
- **F3:** git's command-line `--cleanup` and `--no-status` flags are invisible to the hooks. I'd add that to the docs paragraph, and draft a "Known gap" line for the PR description for you to approve before I post it.
- **F6:** rewrite the 60-line docs paragraph as a short list of rules.

  opens no editor (`-m`/`-F` without `-e`, `--no-edit`, `-C`). The source

  comment block (below the diff with `-v`, where git discards it), and a
